summary: Order submit failures (~30%) and 504s began at ~10:50 UTC, coinciding with order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) but NOT caused by it. The error chain is: order-service -> exchange-gateway -> external exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example). exchange-gateway's logs show 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable', with its upstream_error_rate jumping 0.3%->~46% and upstream_latency 120ms->~9.3s. exchange-gateway itself is healthy (no deploy, no config change, CPU ~30%, memory ~44%, 0 restarts, request_rate flat ~270/s), so the fault originates at the external partner. Critically, market-data-service -- an independent caller of exchange-gateway with no relation to order-service -- also degraded at the same 10:50 onset (0.2%->6.6%), and error rates persisted well after the order-service rollback at 11:16. The rollback of dep-5333 is therefore ineffective; the root cause is the external exchange partner dependency failure (matching historical HIST-103).

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner API degradation (dependency_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange provider api.exchange-partner.example began failing at ~11:01 UTC (connect timeouts after 5000ms and 503 Service Unavailable), causing exchange-gateway upstream errors (~46%), which propagated as 504s to exchange-gateway's callers order-service and market-data-service, and onward to api-gateway. The order-service v2.15.2 deploy is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: external exchange partner api.exchange-partner.example starts timing out (5000ms) and returning 503 at ~11:01
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate 0.3%->46% and upstream_latency 120ms->9.3s; circuit breaker opens
order-service emits 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504' and error_rate 0.2%->31%, latency p99 ->5.3s
independent caller market-data-service and upstream api-gateway degrade at the same 10:50 onset, confirming a shared downstream fault

assumptions: exchange-api has no telemetry (vendor external, has_telemetry=false), so partner-side evidence is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics/logs
no infra change on the network path to the partner occurred

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 deploy caused failures (bad_deployment)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The dep-5333 order-service release introduced a fault that caused order submit 504s.

causal_chain.claim: deploy dep-5333 at 10:48 introduced the failure

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rollback at 11:16 did not restore service (errors persist to 12:58); the errors are explicit upstream timeouts to the external partner, not order-service code paths; the independent caller market-data-service degraded at the same onset; and exchange-gateway shows the partner fault with no deploy of its own. Timing coincidence only.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Exchange-gateway resource exhaustion or saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway ran out of CPU/memory/connections or saturated its capacity, causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU flat ~30%, memory flat ~44%, restarts 0, request_rate flat ~270 req/s; errors are upstream-attributed (upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency), not local resource signals.

facts.statement: order-service error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~31% at the 10:50 bucket and persisted.
order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) deployed 10:48 and rolled back 11:16; errors did not stop.
order-service ERROR logs are exclusively 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'.
exchange-gateway error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~44% at the same 10:50 onset.
exchange-gateway logs show 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable'.
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate ~46% and upstream_latency ~9.3s at onset.
exchange-gateway internal resources healthy: CPU ~30%, memory ~44%, restarts 0, request_rate flat.
exchange-gateway had zero deployments and zero config changes in the window.
market-data-service, an independent exchange-gateway caller, degraded at the same 10:50 onset.
pricing-engine stayed healthy (error rate ~0.2%) despite cfg-2290.
Historical HIST-103 is a partner-side exchange outage causing the same symptoms.

assumptions: exchange-api has no telemetry (has_telemetry=false), so the partner-side fault is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream metrics and logs.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the order-service rollback as the fix and check status/status page of external exchange partner api.exchange-partner.example; engage the vendor.
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors persist after rollback and originate from partner connect timeouts/503s.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over exchange traffic to the secondary exchange route (as done in HIST-103) if available.
recommended_actions.rationale: Removes dependence on the degraded partner.

recommended_actions.action: Tune exchange-gateway circuit breaker/timeout behavior and queue/shed order submissions to protect callers during partner degradation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Circuit breaker opened but failures still propagated as 504s to callers.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry/alerting on the external partner dependency and reduce the 5000ms connect timeout so degradation is detected earlier.
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-api has no telemetry; degradation was only visible indirectly.
